sources.title: People’s Republic of China: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Staff Report (Country Report 26/044)
sources.observedPeriod: Staff discussions ended 2025-12-10; report completed 2026-01-28; 2025 assessment and 2026–31 projections
sources.revision: 2026 Article IV vintage; staff report is a diagnosis/projection, not a causal estimate
sources.units: Mixed; report-specific tables include percent of GDP, growth rates, RMB and financial-sector ratios
sources.relevance: Property/LG finance/debt-overhang and weak domestic demand, policy/external offsets, demographics; anchor source across all China mechanisms.

sources.title: Statistical Communiqué of the PRC on 2025 National Economic and Social Development
sources.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
sources.observedPeriod: Calendar 2025; population at 2025 year-end
sources.revision: Preliminary national accounts and annual statistics; subsequent benchmark/revision possible
sources.units: RMB, percent, persons (tables commonly in 10,000 persons), per-thousand rates
sources.relevance: Observed macro, household consumption contribution, prices, population/age composition and labor; use category definitions as printed.

sources.title: September 2026 Consumer Price Index release
sources.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
sources.observedPeriod: September 2026; monthly and year-to-date through September
sources.revision: 2026 CPI rebased to 2025; release published 09:30 China time on cutoff date
sources.units: Percent m/m, y/y and Jan–Sep average; index and expenditure weights
sources.relevance: Latest available consumer-price release at cutoff; not evidence of broad GDP/asset-price deflation; pair with PPI/GDP deflator.

sources.title: Communiqué of the 1% National Population Sample Survey in 2025
sources.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
sources.observedPeriod: Population estimate from 2025 1% sample survey
sources.revision: Sample-survey estimate; differs in scope/age bins from annual statistical communiqué and is not a directly interchangeable revision
sources.units: Persons (millions) and population shares (%)
sources.relevance: Demographic cohort stock and age structure; supports alternate current population vintage with survey basis explicitly retained.

sources.title: Preliminary Balance of Payments for Q4 and full year 2025
sources.observedPeriod: 2025 annual and 2025-Q4 flows
sources.revision: Preliminary release; superseded/revised by SAFE March 27, 2026 BOP release; includes net errors and omissions in reported capital/financial balance
sources.units: RMB billion, USD billion and SDR billion
sources.relevance: External current, capital and financial-account flow categories; shows why a current-account surplus does not mechanically mean capital inflow.

sources.title: Balance of Payments, Q4 and full year 2025 (revised tables)
sources.observedPeriod: Quarterly series since 2019; annual 2025
sources.revision: SAFE says quarterly BOP since 2019 revised using latest data; report financial-account breakdowns by sector and maturity
sources.units: RMB 100 million, USD 100 million and SDR 100 million
sources.relevance: Current-account and capital/financial transaction flows; use latest vintage rather than Feb preliminary summary.

sources.title: International Investment Position at end-2025
sources.observedPeriod: Positions at 2025 year-end
sources.revision: SAFE revised quarterly IIP from 2024 onward and added year-end sector/maturity breakdowns; stock positions affected by valuation as well as transactions
sources.units: USD 100 million or SDR 100 million; end-period stocks
sources.relevance: External asset/liability stocks, instruments, sectors and maturities; do not equate net external assets or reserves with liquid private-sector capacity.

sources.title: SAFE official data and statistics portal (BOP, IIP, external debt, reserves, FX settlement and bank cross-border receipts)
sources.observedPeriod: Series include monthly 2026 releases, 2025 annual data, and quarterly through 2026-Q2 depending on table
sources.revision: Living data index; listed table releases are not a single consistent vintage; selected portal tables updated 2026-09-29
sources.units: Series-specific; flow and stock units differ by table
sources.relevance: Primary entry point for availability and extraction of external flows, reserve assets, gross external debt and banking/currency channels; data definition must be captured at table level.

sources.title: Loan Prime Rate formation and benchmark lending-rate framework
sources.observedPeriod: Framework as posted; benchmark formed from quoting banks and reported by National Interbank Funding Center
sources.revision: Living methodology page; access date 2026-10-14
sources.units: Percent annualized; LPR tenor-specific benchmark
sources.relevance: Instrument definitions for onshore RMB loan pricing; LPR is a benchmark/reference, not each borrower’s effective rate or a single policy rate.

sources.title: Loan Prime Rate quotation for September 2026
sources.publisher: National Interbank Funding Center, reported by State Council of China
sources.revision: Monthly fixing; superseded by later fixing only after 2026-10-20 (outside cutoff)
sources.units: Percent per year: 1-year and over-5-year LPR
sources.relevance: Latest onshore lending benchmark available by cutoff; interpret alongside actual bank/sector loan pricing and PBoC operations.

sources.title: China 2023 Article IV, Box 4: Balance Sheet Deleveraging in China
sources.observedPeriod: Firm/household balance-sheet evidence mainly through 2023-Q3
sources.revision: 2023 Article IV vintage; mixed administrative and commercial firm data, not 2026 data
sources.units: Debt-to-asset ratios (%); survey/administrative measures and report-specific ratios
sources.relevance: Material counterevidence: did not find widespread deleveraging by healthy firms/households; localized property/LGFV stress, precautionary saving and weak confidence are alternative channels.

sources.title: People’s Republic of China: 2024 Article IV Consultation, Staff Report (Country Report 24/258)
sources.observedPeriod: Assessment largely using 2023 outcomes and 2024 outlook
sources.revision: 2024 report vintage; corporate debt/household debt values are not current baselines
sources.units: Percent of GDP, debt ratios, growth and price statistics
sources.relevance: Property and LGFV debt-service/asset-quality vulnerabilities; household savings and balance-sheet counterevidence; historical ratios only.

sources.title: Assessing Vulnerabilities of China’s Corporate Sector (Country Report 24/276, Selected Issues)
sources.observedPeriod: Firm debt, profitability and financing-source evidence through 2024-Q1
sources.revision: IMF staff analysis using BIS/firm datasets; LGFV perimeter and firm-data coverage limit interpretation
sources.units: Debt as percent of GDP; financing shares (%) and corporate ratios
sources.relevance: Domestic/onshore finance reliance and concentration of corporate/LGFV risk; older matched exposure vintage and not a causal external shock estimate.

sources.title: Report on the implementation of the 2025 central and local budgets (local debt risk measures)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Finance of the People’s Republic of China
sources.observedPeriod: Debt swap issuance and implementation during 2025; report to 2026 legislative session
sources.revision: Annual budget implementation report; policy-reported authorization and completion; does not consolidate all LGFV liabilities
sources.units: RMB trillion/billion, debt quota and annual fiscal flows
sources.relevance: Official record of debt replacement as refinancing/term-cost relief and risk management; replacement does not itself erase consolidated public-sector obligations.

sources.title: Locational Banking Statistics: cross-border positions involving China
sources.observedPeriod: Quarterly, coverage through 2026-Q1 in portal snapshot
sources.revision: BIS data are revised; residence vs nationality tables differ; select counterparty China and bank reporting jurisdiction in export
sources.units: US dollars; stocks/outstanding positions and transaction-adjusted changes depend on measure
sources.relevance: Cross-border bank claims/positions to test offshore creditor channels; not onshore RMB credit, FDI, portfolio flows or total Chinese corporate funding.

sources.title: Macroprudential policy as a blunt instrument: evidence from the Japanese credit restriction episodes
sources.publisher: Bank for International Settlements, Working Paper 536
sources.observedPeriod: Japan quantitative credit restriction episodes and subsequent macro/financial outcomes
sources.revision: Working paper; historical episode-specific quasi-experimental identification, not a China forecast coefficient
sources.units: Study-specific credit restriction, lending, real estate and balance-sheet measures
sources.relevance: Scholarly causal identification for one Japan policy episode; useful historical comparison and evidence that credit allocation tools spill beyond targets.

sources.title: The costs of deflations: a historical perspective
sources.publisher: Bank for International Settlements, BIS Quarterly Review
sources.observedPeriod: Historical deflation episodes across countries; analysis published 2015
sources.revision: BIS Quarterly Review, March 2015 issue; exact publication day not verified. Historical sample and episode definitions; distinguish consumer-price from asset-price deflation.
sources.units: Annual price changes and real GDP growth, study-specific
sources.relevance: Counterweight to mechanical debt-deflation claims: goods-price deflation has mixed growth association; asset-price collapses pose clearer collateral/wealth risk.

sources.title: Debt reduction after crises
sources.publisher: Bank for International Settlements, BIS Quarterly Review
sources.observedPeriod: 20 systemic banking crises and post-crisis debt/GDP paths through historical sample
sources.revision: Descriptive cross-crisis sample; average is not a causal estimate or prediction for China
sources.units: Percentage points of GDP and episode counts
sources.relevance: Useful for historical debt repair pathways; selection, denominator effects and crisis comparability limit transport.

sources.title: Monetary Policy Under the Zero Interest Rate Constraint and Balance Sheet Adjustment
sources.publisher: Bank of Japan, Institute for Monetary and Economic Studies Discussion Paper 2001-E-1
sources.observedPeriod: Japan monetary policy and balance-sheet adjustment in the 1990s/early 2000s
sources.revision: Historical research discussion paper; episode and model vintage, not a consensus forecast
sources.units: Japan interest rates, money/credit and balance-sheet variables, paper-specific
sources.relevance: Primary central-bank scholarly analysis of policy transmission when private balance-sheet adjustment constrains monetary easing; contrast institution/capital structure before analogy.

sources.title: China’s Balance of Payments, Q2 and first half 2026
sources.observedPeriod: Q2 and first half 2026; quarterly and half-year BOP flows
sources.revision: Official 2026 Q2/H1 vintage; BOP flows, not IIP stocks. SAFE report says historical revision details are table-specific.
sources.units: RMB billion, USD billion and SDR billion; quarterly flow values

sources.title: China’s International Investment Position at end-June 2026
sources.observedPeriod: End-June 2026 stock positions; direct, portfolio, derivatives, other investment and reserve assets/liabilities
sources.revision: Latest verified IIP vintage available at cutoff; positions include valuation effects and are not transaction flows.
sources.units: USD billion; end-period stock

sources.title: China’s External Debt Data at end-June 2026
sources.observedPeriod: End-June 2026 external debt by institutional sector, debt instrument and original maturity
sources.revision: Official SAFE gross external-debt position; short/long split uses contractual original maturity, not remaining maturity. Excludes Hong Kong SAR, Macao SAR and Taiwan Province of China.
sources.units: RMB billion and USD billion; end-period stock

sources.title: SCIO press conference transcript on monetary policy and financial statistics, first half 2026
sources.publisher: State Council Information Office (SCIO), quoting People’s Bank of China (PBOC) officials
sources.observedPeriod: End-June 2026 financing stocks, H1 2026 financing flows, and June 2026 weighted-average new-loan rates
sources.revision: Official government press conference transcript; preliminary financial aggregates and PBOC spokesperson statements. Rates are weighted averages for newly issued loans, not borrower-specific all-in costs.
sources.units: RMB trillion or billion; year-on-year percent; annualized loan-rate percent

sources.title: Report on implementation of China’s 2025 central and local budgets
sources.publisher: Ministry of Finance of the People’s Republic of China
sources.observedPeriod: 2025 debt-resolution program execution and fiscal implementation
sources.revision: Government report; reports 2025 debt-swap bond issuance completed and qualitative interest-cost/debt-service relief. It does not provide a consolidated LGFV maturity or loss perimeter.
sources.units: RMB trillion for bond issuance; qualitative outcomes

sources.title: Industrial Producer Price Indexes in August 2026
sources.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
sources.observedPeriod: August 2026 monthly and year-on-year industrial PPI; January-August average
sources.revision: 2026 series uses 2025 base period; PPI measures first-sale prices of industrial products and is not GDP deflator or household cost of living.
sources.units: Percent month-on-month and year-on-year

sources.title: Investment in Real Estate Development from January to August 2026
sources.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
sources.observedPeriod: January-August 2026 cumulative real-estate development activity, sales, inventory and funding flows; end-August inventory stock
sources.revision: Comparable year-on-year rates reflect revisions to prior-period data; development-funding indicators are cumulative cash-flow categories, not developer balance sheets or presale completion obligations.
sources.units: RMB billion; million square metres; percent year-on-year; end-period inventory stock

sources.title: People’s Republic of China: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Staff Report, Country Report 26/044
sources.observedPeriod: 2025 estimates and medium-term projections; fiscal and augmented government perimeter; staff discussions ended 2025-12-10
sources.revision: IMF staff estimate/projection, not official Chinese debt statistics or causal identification. Augmented debt includes government-guided funds and LGFV activity; annex explicitly defines perimeter and estimates.
sources.units: Percent of GDP for debt/fiscal series; RMB billion for fiscal table

sources.title: Foreign Exchange Receipts and Payments Data for First Half 2026 — Press Conference Transcript
sources.observedPeriod: H1 2026 cross-border receipts/payments, FX settlements, capital-account facilitation and regulatory channels
sources.revision: SAFE/SCIO transcript; describes policy tools and flows but not an independent measure of control effectiveness or circumvention.
sources.units: USD trillion; percentages; policy descriptions

sources.title: SAFE time-series workbook: Balance of Payments of China (annual and quarterly; revised through Q2 2026)
sources.observedPeriod: Annual BOP 2010–2025 and quarterly BOP 2010Q1–2026Q2; includes instrument detail and sector/maturity rows where reported
sources.revision: Downloaded SAFE workbook linked from official BOP Data and Statistics page. Annual USD worksheet, 2025 column Q; BOP sign convention: positive asset value=net decrease and negative=net increase; positive liability=net increase, negative=net decrease. The workbook displays slash markers rather than numerical values in some 2025 sector/maturity subrows; these were not imputed.
sources.units: USD 100 million (annual USD worksheet), converted to USD billion by dividing by 10

sources.title: Producer Price Index for Industrial Products in September 2026
sources.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
sources.observedPeriod: September 2026; monthly and year-on-year industrial PPI
sources.revision: NBS release available 09:30 China Standard Time on evidence cutoff date. Archived HTML response; table category 生活资料 is living materials/consumer goods.
sources.units: Percent month-on-month and year-on-year
sources.relevance: Corrects the false assertion that August 2026 remained latest at cutoff; September headline industrial PPI +5.0% y/y and +1.2% m/m; living-materials PPI -0.1% y/y.

sources.title: China debt service ratio, private non-financial sector, BIS WS_DSR 1.0 Q:CN:P
sources.observedPeriod: Quarterly 1999-Q1 to 2026-Q1; China private non-financial sector
sources.revision: Official bulk CSV snapshot dated 14 September 2026. Exported series code Q:CN:P; no China household-only row in the topic CSV.
sources.units: Percent of income available for debt service
sources.relevance: Exports latest public China private non-financial-sector DSR; composite is not household-only and is not interchangeable with debt stock or credit flows.

sources.title: Financial Institutions RMB Credit Balance Sheet
sources.publisher: People’s Bank of China, Survey and Statistics Department
sources.observedPeriod: Monthly balance sheet; latest populated month November 2025
sources.revision: Official one-page PDF, table units RMB 100 million. Institutional perimeter includes PBOC, banking depository and non-depository institutions; December 2025 columns were blank in this release. The attachment path includes 2025/12, but exact public posting day was not independently verified.
sources.units: RMB 100 million; stocks at month end
sources.relevance: Household loan/deposit stocks and short/medium-long credit composition, not loan-purpose collateral-level mortgage stock. Latest populated observation is older than the 2026 H1 flow release.

sources.title: China Vanke investor announcements index
sources.observedPeriod: Issuer announcement list; includes 2026 Interim Report dated 16 September 2026
sources.revision: Issuer site page returned anti-bot slider in direct local request; search-indexed issuer listing locates the report but not its tables.
sources.relevance: Primary issuer source for interim-report existence/date; direct report retrieval was blocked during closure.

sources.title: China Vanke Co., Ltd. 2026 Interim Report (issuer report text mirror)
sources.publisher: FinancialFilings.com (secondary text mirror of China Vanke Co., Ltd. report)
sources.observedPeriod: Consolidated financial position as at 30 June 2026; six months ended 30 June 2026
sources.revision: Transcribed report-text mirror. Issuer listing independently shows report date; mirror states reviewed interim statements (not audited), approved 27 Aug 2026. Direct HTTP request to mirror returned 403; values were extracted from indexed/web-accessible report text. Treat as secondary-located figures pending primary-host validation.
sources.units: RMB thousand in statements; normalized to RMB billion in closure table
sources.relevance: Issuer group perimeter balance-sheet and financing illustration, not representative sector total. Does not disclose full foreign/onshore funding split.
